steps.intent: Our primary objective is to strictly limit any extension of the obsolete cross-border mechanism to six months, while demanding respect for Syrian sovereignty, substantial progress on cross-line aid delivery, and robust expansion of early recovery funding. We also aim to compel the Secretariat to formally report on the devastating humanitarian consequences of Western unilateral coercive measures. The main points of contention will be the six-month timeframe—opposed by Western delegations who insist on a 12-month or 9-month mandate—and our operative paragraph demanding a special report on unilateral sanctions.

messages.Albania: Albania firmly supports the tireless efforts of the humanitarian co-penholders, Switzerland and Brazil, to secure a predictable and sustainable 12-month extension of the cross-border mechanism. A six-month authorization severely undermines humanitarian planning ahead of the harsh winter months, and we cannot accept the insertion of politically motivated language on unilateral coercive measures. Humanitarian aid must not be held hostage to political agendas, and this Council must prioritize the survival of over 4 million vulnerable Syrians.
messages.Brazil: As co-penholder on the Syrian humanitarian file alongside Switzerland, Brazil remains steadfast in our commitment to ensuring uninterrupted, life-saving aid to millions of civilians in north-west Syria. A six-month renewal expiring in January poses grave operational and humanitarian risks during the peak of winter, which is why we continue to advocate for a minimum nine-month extension to provide predictability for humanitarian actors. We urge the Russian delegation to engage constructively on these adjustments and on contentious provisions so that the Council can maintain unity and renew this vital mechanism.
messages.China: China fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the Russian Federation, which properly balances the urgent humanitarian needs of the Syrian people with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We appreciate the draft's emphasis on advancing cross-line deliveries, scaling up early recovery projects, and specifically addressing the adverse humanitarian impact of unilateral coercive measures. China is ready to vote in favour of this text and calls on all Council members to bridge differences through constructive dialogue.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador reaffirms its full confidence in and support for the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, in guiding the Council's efforts to ensure unhindered humanitarian access to all Syrians in need. A longer mandate of at least nine to twelve months is essential to give humanitarian agencies the operational predictability needed to save lives, especially during the harsh winter months. We urge the penholder to focus strictly on humanitarian imperatives and remove divisive political language regarding unilateral coercive measures.
messages.France: France cannot accept a draft that weaponizes humanitarian assistance and introduces unacceptable political elements regarding unilateral sanctions. Operational predictability requires a minimum 12-month mandate so that humanitarian actors are not plunged into uncertainty in the middle of winter. The Council must rally behind the compromise established by the humanitarian co-penholders rather than text designed to undermine the cross-border lifeline.
messages.Gabon: Gabon emphasizes that humanitarian assistance must remain strictly depoliticized and guided by the principles of humanity, neutrality, and impartiality. A six-month renewal provides insufficient predictability for humanitarian partners on the ground, especially with the impending winter. We urge the penholder and all Council members to redouble efforts toward a unified compromise that preserves this vital humanitarian lifeline.
messages.Ghana: Ghana stresses that Council action on the humanitarian file must prioritize the needs of vulnerable Syrians and ensure operational predictability for UN agencies, which a six-month mandate expiring in mid-winter severely compromises. We encourage the penholder to explore a compromise duration of at least nine months to provide adequate planning runway for humanitarian actors. In addition, we urge flexibility regarding divisive language on unilateral coercive measures in order to bridge differences and maintain Council unity on this critical humanitarian lifeline.
messages.Japan: Japan underscores that ensuring predictable and uninterrupted humanitarian assistance to millions of people in north-west Syria is a critical humanitarian imperative. In line with the Secretary-General's recommendation and the appeals of humanitarian organizations, a 12-month extension is essential to provide operational certainty, especially during the harsh winter months. Furthermore, we believe the Council must maintain a strictly humanitarian focus and avoid introducing controversial language regarding unilateral coercive measures.
messages.Malta: Malta firmly supports the efforts of the humanitarian co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, and emphasizes that Council action must be guided strictly by humanitarian imperatives. A 12-month extension is indispensable to provide humanitarian actors with operational stability and avoid an aid disruption in the middle of winter. We cannot support the introduction of contentious political language regarding unilateral coercive measures, nor provisions that undermine the critical cross-border lifeline.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique stresses that humanitarian assistance must be depoliticized and guided solely by the imperative to alleviate the suffering of the Syrian people. We support the continuation of the cross-border mechanism alongside expanded cross-line deliveries and early recovery projects, but operational predictability requires a renewal period longer than six months. We urge all delegations, particularly the penholder and the co-penholders Brazil and Switzerland, to work collaboratively towards a consensus text that avoids Council paralysis.
messages.Switzerland: As co-penholder on the Syrian humanitarian file alongside Brazil, Switzerland stresses that humanitarian operations require predictability and operational continuity, making a 12-month extension critical—particularly as vulnerable populations face harsh winter conditions. A six-month renewal falls short of the clear operational needs identified by the Secretary-General and humanitarian partners on the ground. We also caution against introducing politically contentious language on unilateral coercive measures, which risks Council unity on what must remain a purely humanitarian mandate.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates emphasizes that meeting the dire humanitarian needs of the brotherly Syrian people must transcend political differences. We strongly welcome the focus on expanding early recovery projects—especially electricity and demining—as well as advancing cross-line modalities in full respect of Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity. To avoid a Council deadlock that would imperil humanitarian access, we urge constructive flexibility on the mandate's duration and bridging language that can secure the widest possible Council unity.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support this draft, which disregards the unequivocal assessment of the Secretary-General and humanitarian organizations that a 12-month renewal is essential for operational certainty and meeting the desperate needs of 4.1 million Syrians through the winter. Moreover, the injection of politicized text and reporting demands regarding unilateral coercive measures is entirely unacceptable and misrepresents targeted sanctions that already contain broad humanitarian carve-outs. We urge the Council to respect the process led by the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, rather than pursue divisive drafts that undermine life-saving aid.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft, which disregards the clear appeals of the Secretary-General, UN humanitarian agencies, and NGOs on the ground who have repeatedly stated that a minimum of 12 months is essential for effective humanitarian planning and procurement. A six-month extension would once again leave millions of vulnerable Syrians facing a humanitarian cliff in the dead of winter. Furthermore, the cynical injection of politicized language on unilateral coercive measures is entirely unacceptable and deters from the Council's core humanitarian responsibility.

messages.Albania: Humanitarian assistance must never be politicized or held hostage to extraneous political agendas. A six-month mandate severely disrupts the operational predictability and planning required by humanitarian actors to support over four million people in northwest Syria. Because our red lines on duration and the inappropriate introduction of unilateral coercive measures have been completely ignored, Albania cannot support this draft.
messages.Brazil: As co-penholder alongside Switzerland, Brazil remains convinced that a nine-month extension represents the necessary middle ground to guarantee humanitarian predictability throughout the harsh winter months. We regret that our proposals to reflect the indispensable role of cross-border operations alongside cross-line efforts were not accommodated. Under the current formulation, which lacks Council consensus, Brazil cannot support the draft and will abstain.
messages.China: China fully supports the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation, which strikes an appropriate balance by respecting Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity while addressing urgent humanitarian needs. The text rightly underscores the temporary nature of the cross-border mechanism, promotes the expansion of cross-line relief, advances early recovery projects, and properly highlights the adverse humanitarian impact of unilateral coercive measures. We encourage all Council members to support this balanced draft.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador reiterates its full support for the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, and stresses the necessity of ensuring predictable and uninterrupted humanitarian access for the millions of civilians in north-west Syria through a longer extension. We cannot support the inclusion of divisive political elements, such as unilateral coercive measures, which distract from the core humanitarian objective of this mechanism. Unless the text reflects a genuine consensus and ensures operational predictability without prejudicing cross-border aid, Ecuador will not be in a position to vote in favour.
messages.France: France cannot accept a text that injects controversial political language on unilateral coercive measures and disregards the clear appeals of the Secretary-General and humanitarian agencies for a 12-month renewal. A six-month mandate in the middle of winter creates intolerable uncertainty for millions of civilians in north-west Syria, while cross-border aid remains completely irreplaceable. If our red lines regarding unilateral coercive measures and the duration of the mandate are not respected, France will vote against this draft.
messages.Gabon: Gabon regrets that our calls for a longer mandate and consensus-oriented language were not integrated into this revision. A six-month authorization falls short of providing the necessary predictability for humanitarian operations heading into the harsh winter months, and retaining contentious provisions on unilateral coercive measures prevents Council unity. Without an inclusive compromise that bridges divisions and secures broad support, Gabon will not be able to vote in favour of the draft in its current form.
messages.Ghana: Ghana reiterates that ensuring operational predictability for humanitarian agencies through the winter requires a duration beyond six months, and we strongly encourage exploring a compromise of at least nine months. Additionally, we remain concerned that divisive language on unilateral coercive measures detracts from the Council's shared humanitarian objective and impedes broad consensus. In the absence of revisions reflecting these essential compromises, Ghana will not be able to support the draft resolution in its current form and will abstain.
messages.Japan: Japan remains convinced that a 12-month extension of the cross-border mechanism is essential to provide humanitarian actors with the operational predictability needed to assist millions of Syrians in desperate need. Furthermore, addressing the urgent humanitarian crisis should not be conflated with political issues, and we cannot accept references to unilateral coercive measures in this context. Unless these key humanitarian concerns are accommodated, Japan will not be in a position to vote in favour of this text.
messages.Malta: Malta reiterates that a 12-month extension is essential to provide humanitarian actors with the operational predictability required to assist millions of Syrians in desperate need. Furthermore, we maintain our strong principled objection to introducing politicized language and reporting mandates on unilateral coercive measures into a purely humanitarian resolution. Without meaningful movement on these critical concerns, Malta will not be in a position to support this draft resolution.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique emphasizes that preserving a predictable and uninterrupted humanitarian lifeline for the Syrian people must remain our collective priority, particularly across the harsh winter months. A nine-month extension remains the most viable bridge to ensure operational certainty for humanitarian agencies while addressing Council dynamics. We urge the penholder to show flexibility on the duration and on divisive language to allow the Council to unite behind this critical text.
messages.Switzerland: As co-penholder of the Syrian humanitarian file alongside Brazil, Switzerland emphasizes that humanitarian operations require predictability, particularly to avoid an expiration in the middle of winter; we therefore strongly urge a compromise extension of at least nine months. Furthermore, introducing contentious and politicized language on unilateral coercive measures distracts from the strictly humanitarian nature of this mechanism. Unless the text provides adequate operational duration and addresses these core concerns, Switzerland cannot support the draft and will abstain.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates appreciates the penholder's constructive incorporation of language emphasizing early recovery projects, particularly electricity and humanitarian mine action, as well as cross-line delivery. However, our primary objective remains achieving a unified Council outcome that guarantees predictable, sustained, and depoliticized aid to the Syrian people. As the current draft does not bridge the existing divides among Council members regarding mandate duration and reporting mechanisms, we cannot support it in its current form and will abstain unless consensus-based adjustments are made.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot accept a text that disregards the clear humanitarian imperative articulated by the Secretary-General and UN agencies for a 12-month extension, which is essential to avoid plunging millions of vulnerable Syrians into uncertainty in the dead of winter. We also firmly reject the politicization of this lifeline through unwarranted language and reporting mandates on unilateral sanctions. If the penholder continues to refuse these fundamental changes, the United Kingdom will vote against this draft.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot accept a draft that weaponizes aid and injects politicized grievances regarding unilateral sanctions into a purely humanitarian resolution. A six-month authorization would needlessly create an aid cliff in the middle of winter, running contrary to the explicit appeals of the Secretary-General, UN agencies, and humanitarian NGOs. If the penholder refuses to remove the unacceptable provisions on unilateral coercive measures and align the mandate duration with humanitarian needs, the United States will vote against this text.

steps.summary: The Russian Federation maintains its principled draft providing a six-month extension of the Bab al-Hawa crossing alongside essential language on unilateral coercive measures, early recovery, and cross-line assistance. We categorically reject Western demands to prolong an erosion of Syrian sovereignty or suppress the truth about the humanitarian toll of illegal unilateral sanctions. If Western permanent members vote down this balanced solution, the responsibility for closing the cross-border mechanism lies squarely with them.

before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation has put forward a draft resolution that offers a viable, realistic and compromise-based approach to extending the cross-border mechanism for six months, until 10 January 2024. 

Our draft addresses the real, acute humanitarian needs of the Syrian people without discrimination or politicization. It contains critical provisions on early recovery projects, demands genuine progress on cross-line humanitarian deliveries to all parts of Syria, and requests an objective assessment of the detrimental impact of unilateral coercive measures—illegal sanctions that continue to strangle the Syrian economy and impede humanitarian response. 

We have heard repeatedly that the mechanism is essential for the people of north-west Syria. If Council members truly care about maintaining humanitarian aid deliveries rather than political grandstanding, they have the opportunity to support our text. A vote against our draft resolution will demonstrate who is genuinely interested in helping Syrians and who is merely using humanitarian aid as leverage for geopolitical interests. We urge all Council members to vote in favour of our draft.
before.United States of America:
The United States will vote against this draft resolution. Just moments ago, Russia used its veto to block a compromise resolution painstakingly negotiated by the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, supported by the humanitarian community, the Secretary-General, and the vast majority of this Council. That compromise would have provided a nine-month extension to ensure predictable, life-saving assistance reaches over four million vulnerable Syrians through the winter.

Having just killed that lifeline, Russia now presents a cynical text designed not to help the Syrian people, but to serve its own political agenda. A six-month authorization creates logistical chaos, making it impossible for humanitarian agencies to plan, procure, and contract effectively. Moreover, this draft injects extraneous and politicized language regarding unilateral sanctions, attempting to deflect blame from the Syrian regime's own brutality and obstruction. We cannot and will not support a text that holds millions of Syrian civilians hostage to Moscow's political demands.

after.Albania:
Albania deeply regrets the failure of the Security Council today to extend the cross-border humanitarian mechanism for north-west Syria. 

We want to express our sincere appreciation to the co-penholders, Switzerland and Brazil, for their tireless, inclusive, and transparent efforts to craft a workable compromise. 

Today is another sad day for the Syrian people and for this Council. Once again, the Council was prevented from fulfilling its humanitarian duty by a single permanent member using its veto against the overwhelming majority of Council members, against the clear recommendation of the Secretary-General, and against the desperate appeals of humanitarian organizations on the ground. 

Over four million people in north-west Syria, the vast majority of them women and children, depend on the cross-border mechanism for their daily survival. Following years of conflict and the devastating earthquakes earlier this year, their needs are higher than ever. A 12-month authorization was what humanitarian actors needed to ensure predictable planning and procurement. The nine-month proposal put forward by the co-penholders was already a significant compromise, specifically designed to ensure that life-saving assistance would continue uninterrupted through the harsh winter months. That compromise was blocked.

Albania abstained on the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. A six-month extension expiring in the dead of winter is completely inadequate and creates unbearable operational uncertainty for humanitarian actors and the vulnerable populations they serve. Moreover, the draft introduced political elements that distract from the purely humanitarian objective of saving lives. 

Humanitarian assistance must never be politicized, instrumentalized, or held hostage to geopolitical considerations. Millions of Syrian lives are at stake. We urge all Council members to put the plight of the Syrian people first and to work urgently to find a solution to maintain this vital humanitarian lifeline.
after.Brazil:
I thank you, Mr. President.

Brazil deeply regrets that the Security Council has been unable to reach an agreement today to renew the authorization for the cross-border humanitarian mechanism in north-west Syria. 

As co-penholders on this critical file alongside Switzerland, we have spared no effort over the past several weeks to bridge differences, listen carefully to all Council members, and craft a balanced, compromise text that reflected the humanitarian imperative. We proposed a nine-month extension, in close consultation with the United Nations humanitarian agencies and humanitarian actors on the ground, as a pragmatic middle ground to ensure that millions of vulnerable Syrians, especially women and children, would not be left without vital, life-saving aid as winter approaches. It is profoundly disheartening that this compromise was blocked earlier today.

With regard to the draft resolution just voted on, Brazil decided to abstain. While we have always maintained that keeping cross-border access open through Bab al-Hawa is indispensable, and while we recognize the importance of elements such as early recovery projects and expanding cross-line operations, the draft presented by the Russian Federation failed to garner the necessary consensus and broad support within the Council. 

Throughout our tenure as co-penholders, Brazil has consistently advocated that humanitarian assistance must be guided strictly by the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence. It must never be subordinated to political considerations or geopolitical divides. Millions of Syrian civilians depend on the Council's ability to act responsibly and unitedly to alleviate their suffering.

Despite this deeply disappointing outcome, Brazil remains firmly committed to the Syrian people. Together with Switzerland, we will not give up. We stand ready to re-engage immediately with all members of the Security Council to explore every possible pathway to preserve this humanitarian lifeline and find a viable solution that places the needs of the Syrian people above all else.

I thank you.
after.China:
(spoke in Chinese): China regrets that the Security Council was unable to reach a consensus on the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian assistance mechanism to Syria. 

China’s position on the humanitarian situation in Syria is consistent and clear. We always maintain that humanitarian assistance to Syria must fully respect Syria’s sovereignty and the ownership of the Syrian Government. Cross-border assistance is an exceptional and temporary arrangement made under special circumstances, and there must be an accelerated transition toward cross-line assistance, which should eventually become the primary channel for humanitarian relief throughout Syria. At the same time, practical steps must be taken to effectively expand early recovery projects and address humanitarian mine action across the country.

Unilateral coercive measures have long severely undermined Syria’s economic development, disrupted basic livelihoods, and gravely impeded international humanitarian operations and post-earthquake reconstruction. The negative humanitarian impact of unilateral sanctions cannot be overlooked or avoided. Any comprehensive and objective humanitarian response in Syria must address the adverse effects of these unilateral measures and work toward their complete and immediate lifting.

The draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation proposed a six-month extension of the cross-border mechanism, while actively responding to the urgent need to expand cross-line delivery, advance early recovery projects, and assess the impact of unilateral coercive measures. These elements are both legitimate and necessary for addressing the root causes and full picture of Syria’s humanitarian plight. It is regrettable that despite these constructive elements, the draft resolution was not adopted.

Humanitarian issues should not be politicized. Dialogue and consultation remain the only viable way forward to bridge differences and maintain the unity of the Council. China calls on all parties to uphold a constructive approach, take full account of the legitimate concerns of all sides, respect Syria’s sovereignty, and continue to work patiently to find an appropriate solution that genuinely serves the interests and well-being of the Syrian people.
after.France:
*(spoke in French)*

France voted against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.

Just a moment ago, Russia chose once again to isolate itself by vetoing a balanced, compromise text put forward by the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, which was supported by the Secretary-General, United Nations humanitarian agencies, non-governmental organizations on the ground, and 13 members of this Council. That compromise would have provided a nine-month extension to ensure predictable and life-saving assistance through the harsh winter months for more than 4 million people in north-west Syria.

Having blocked that lifeline, Russia attempted to impose an ultimatum on this Council with a draft text that serves only its own political interests and those of the Syrian regime, at the expense of millions of civilians in desperate need. 

France cannot accept such an approach. A six-month mandate creates operational and logistical instability for humanitarian actors who require predictability to plan, procure, and deliver aid efficiently. Furthermore, the Russian text sought to instrumentalize humanitarian aid by introducing extraneous and political language, particularly regarding unilateral sanctions. As we have repeatedly made clear, European and national sanctions target only the perpetrators of atrocities and war crimes; they include robust humanitarian exemptions and do not impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance or medicine. 

The cross-border mechanism authorized by this Council remains an irreplaceable lifeline. Cross-line deliveries, while encouraged, cannot substitute for the scale and scope of cross-border operations. By pushing this text and vetoing the co-penholders' compromise, Russia bears the full and sole responsibility for cutting off vital aid to millions of Syrians.

France will not abandon the Syrian people. We will continue our steadfast humanitarian engagement alongside our European and international partners. At the same time, France’s position remains unchanged: there will be no financing of reconstruction, no normalization, and no lifting of sanctions until a credible, inclusive, and verifiable political process is firmly underway, in full accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan deeply regrets that the Security Council was unable to adopt the draft resolution prepared by the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, due to the use of the veto by a permanent member, despite having received the overwhelming support of Council members.

The cross-border humanitarian mechanism authorized by this Council is an indispensable lifeline for over four million people in north-west Syria who depend on it for their survival, particularly in the aftermath of the devastating earthquakes in February. We express our sincere appreciation to the co-penholders for their tireless and transparent efforts to craft a compromise that sought to address the critical humanitarian needs on the ground.

With regard to the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation, Japan decided to abstain. A six-month extension does not provide the necessary predictability, stability, and operational efficiency required by the United Nations and humanitarian partners to procure and deliver life-saving aid effectively, especially as the harsh winter months approach. Furthermore, the draft did not reflect the broad consensus of the Council.

Humanitarian assistance should never be politicized or held hostage to political considerations. The Council has a responsibility to ensure that life-saving aid reaches vulnerable populations in Syria without disruption. Japan urges all Council members to place the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people first and to continue constructive engagement to find a way forward.

I thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
(spoke in Russian): 

Today, the members of the Security Council have witnessed the true face and priorities of our Western colleagues. 

For weeks, we heard endless lamentations from Washington, London and Paris about the critical need to preserve the cross-border mechanism, about the dire plight of four million Syrians in north-west Syria, and about how any disruption would lead to humanitarian catastrophe. Yet when presented with a concrete, balanced draft resolution that would have immediately extended the cross-border mechanism through the Bab al-Hawa crossing for six months, the United States, the United Kingdom and France chose to vote against it, while others chose to abstain. 

By doing so, the Western troika has clearly shown that their concern for ordinary Syrians is nothing more than hypocritical posturing and political gamesmanship. Their primary goal was not to provide humanitarian aid to people in need, but to preserve an obsolete, temporary arrangement that violates Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, shields terrorists in Idlib, and serves their narrow geopolitical agenda. They refused to acknowledge the reality on the ground, rejected any serious progress on cross-line deliveries from Damascus, opposed genuine early recovery efforts, and deliberately ignored the devastating, criminal impact of their unilateral coercive measures on the Syrian civilian population.

We warned you clearly: if our compromise text was not supported, the cross-border mechanism would simply shut down. You made your choice. You have effectively buried the cross-border mechanism yourselves. Do not attempt to shift the blame onto Russia. The entire responsibility for the closure of the cross-border mechanism falls squarely on the shoulders of the United States and its allies.
after.Switzerland:
I am taking the floor on behalf of Brazil and Switzerland as co-penholders of the humanitarian file on Syria.

We deeply regret that the Security Council was unable to reach an agreement today to extend the mandate of the vital cross-border humanitarian mechanism in north-west Syria.

For weeks, we have worked tirelessly and in good faith, listening carefully to all members of the Council and engaging closely with humanitarian actors on the ground, as well as the Secretary-General, to craft a balanced, compromise text. Our draft resolution, which proposed a nine-month extension, took into account the operational realities and the plea of humanitarian organizations for predictability, especially with the harsh winter ahead, while seeking to address the concerns of all Council members. It received the overwhelming support of thirteen members of this Council. We are deeply disappointed that a veto prevented its adoption.

With regard to the draft resolution just voted upon, Switzerland abstained because it did not represent a genuine compromise capable of uniting the Council, nor did it sufficiently take into account the operational requirements repeatedly voiced by the United Nations and humanitarian agencies. A six-month mandate does not provide the necessary predictability for humanitarian operations, and the text lacked the broad consensus required to ensure the continued functioning of this indispensable lifeline.

Today, humanitarian needs across Syria are higher than ever, further exacerbated by the catastrophic earthquakes of February. More than four million people in north-west Syria depend on cross-border assistance for their daily survival. The Security Council has a collective responsibility towards these vulnerable populations.

Brazil and Switzerland, as co-penholders, will not abandon this responsibility. We remain fully committed to continuing our work with all Council members to bridge differences and urgently find a solution that allows life-saving humanitarian assistance to continue reaching all those in need.
after.United Arab Emirates:
The United Arab Emirates expresses its deep regret that the Security Council was unable today to reach a consensus to renew the cross-border humanitarian aid mechanism in Syria. 

At a time when the Syrian people continue to face catastrophic humanitarian conditions, compounded by the devastating earthquakes earlier this year, our collective focus should have remained squarely on addressing their urgent, life-saving needs rather than political divisions. Millions of Syrians depend on this vital lifeline, and they look to the Council to set aside geopolitical considerations in favour of their basic survival.

We thank the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, for their tireless efforts throughout this negotiation process to reach a balanced, workable compromise that reflected the overwhelming humanitarian priorities on the ground.

The United Arab Emirates voted in favour of the draft resolution presented by the co-penholders earlier today because it provided the necessary predictability and operational stability required by humanitarian agencies to support Syrians ahead of the harsh winter months. We abstained on the draft resolution just voted on, as our primary objective has always been to support a consensus-driven approach that ensures the uninterrupted delivery of aid.

Our position remains clear: humanitarian aid must never be politicized. The delivery of assistance through all modalities—both cross-border and cross-line—must be expanded to reach all Syrians in need, across all parts of the country, without discrimination. At the same time, we must urgently scale up early-recovery projects, including in vital sectors such as water, sanitation, health, education, shelter, and electricity, as well as humanitarian demining, to help the Syrian people build resilience and restore basic livelihoods.

Any sustainable solution must fully respect the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We urge all Council members not to abandon the spirit of dialogue and to redouble their efforts to reach an agreement that puts the humanitarian needs and dignity of the brotherly Syrian people first.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
I thank the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, for their tireless efforts to reach a compromise that would have protected the humanitarian lifeline for millions of vulnerable Syrians. 

The United Kingdom voted against the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. Earlier today, Russia chose to veto a balanced, humanitarian compromise that was supported by the overwhelming majority of Council members, the Secretary-General, and the entire humanitarian community. That compromise had already met Russia halfway by reducing the requested 12-month renewal to nine months. 

Having blocked that effort, Russia then attempted to force upon the Council a text designed not to meet humanitarian needs, but to serve its own political agenda. A six-month mandate is unworkable. It creates operational uncertainty and would expire in January, in the depths of winter, when vulnerable people in north-west Syria need life-saving aid the most. Moreover, the Russian draft sought to inject politicized language on unilateral coercive measures, which are a transparent distraction from the Syrian regime’s own brutality and mismanagement. 

Russia’s actions today demonstrate utter disregard for the lives of the 4.1 million people in north-west Syria who depend on cross-border assistance. Holding life-saving humanitarian assistance hostage to political games is unconscionable.

The United Kingdom will continue to stand with the Syrian people. We remain determined to work with our partners to ensure that humanitarian assistance reaches all those who need it through every available route.
